per_finding.id: H3-r3 workflow block scalars / flow style
per_finding.notes: Honest heredoc/github-script content now passes and two flow forms are caught, but the new block-scalar skip swallows sibling keys of a '- key: |' list item, so continue-on-error and ${{ }} run injection are no longer detected in the most common step shape (issue 1, major). Other flow variants still evade (issue 7).
The three literal forms (./hooks, $PWD/hooks, ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/scripts) now fail; project paths outside hooks/ or scripts/ still pass (issue 8).
H3 is merged into the base; git merge-tree --write-tree 21606d0 8667a48 is clean (tree e1c7b0dc); all 17 invariants PASS on the materialised merge tree.

issues.problem: Regression introduced by this package. The block-scalar skip computes the extent with indent_of(line), which for a list-item line ('      - run: |', '      - name: >-') is the dash column. Every sibling key of that step (indent 8 > 6) is treated as scalar text and skipped, so continue-on-error and ${{ }} in a run line are no longer reported. RUN_KEY already used len(run.group(1)) (the key column) correctly; BLOCK_SCALAR does not. 6dcbc84 reported both; 8667a48 reports nothing.
issues.evidence:
REVF-H3b-probe/dec/wf-fixture/.github/workflows/ci.yml: steps '- run: |
    git status --porcelain --ignored
  continue-on-error: true' and '- name: >-
    Greet
  run: echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}"'. base repo_invariants.py workflow-hardening -> ':14: continue-on-error hides failures', ':17: ${{ }} expression inside a run script' rc=1; head -> rc=0; head check-repo-invariants.sh --check workflow-hardening -> 'PASS workflow-hardening'. Module probe REVF-H3b-probe/dec/scan/wfprobe.py: run_block_then_coe base=[coe] head=[]; name_block_then_coe_and_injection base=[coe, injection] head=[].
issues.suggested_fix: Use the key column as the parent indent, as RUN_KEY does: match r'^(\s*(?:-\s+)?)[^:]+:\s*[|>]' and pass len(group(1)) to block_extent. Add tests: '- run: |' followed by sibling continue-on-error: true, and '- name: >-' followed by a run with ${{ }}, both must fail.

issues.problem: R13-11 is claimed fixed, but the maintainer's home path survives in forms the scrub and the new CI invariant both miss: Cursor's project-dir form 'Users-<name>-projects-...' (no leading dash, so DASHED_HOME misses it) in a shipped runtime script and a planning doc; the lean-ctx form '_Users_<name>_' in 2 run logs; lowercase '/users/<name>/...' and 'users_<name>_projects' in graph.json (normalised labels/ids, 6+ hits); 'file:///Users/<name>/.cursor/...' link URIs inside 2 research PDFs (binary files are skipped). The guard also misses /var/home/<name>, -home-<name>- (Linux Claude project dirs), JSON-escaped \/Users\/<name>, url-encoded %2FUsers%2F<name>, and <user>@<host>.local git default emails ('local' is an allowlisted TLD). Since this repo's own tooling emits the Cursor and lean-ctx forms, future leaks will pass CI.
issues.evidence: python3 -I REVF-H3b-probe/dec/scan/scan.py <worktree>: cursor_dash_users -> .planning/VERIFIER-FAIL-ANALYTICS.md:58, scripts/run-visual-qa-pipeline.sh:11; underscore_users -> .planning/rfl-router-subagent-surfaces-85bf9f09-20260812/deepseek-v4-pro-high-ladder4/launch.nohup.out.attempt2:25, .../opencode-run.log.attempt2:17, graphify-out/graph.json:1; lower_users_home -> graphify-out/graph.json:1. git grep -a: research/2026-07-20-agentic-sdlc-orchestration-landscape-multimarket-final/landscape-report.pdf and .../landscape/landscape-report.pdf. Fixture REVF-H3b-probe/dec/pd/docs/fn.md with 10 such forms (placeholder name) -> personal-data rc=0, no line reported. Real tree: check-repo-invariants 'PASS personal-data'.
issues.suggested_fix: Scrub the listed files (run-visual-qa-pipeline.sh should default to a $HOME-relative or env-provided path; regenerate graph.json with graphify update after the source scrub). Make the home pattern case-insensitive, accept [-_/] separators around Users/home (Users-<n>-, _Users_<n>_, -home-<n>-), cover /var/home, decode \/ and %2F before matching, drop 'local' from the allowlisted TLDs, and scan text-bearing binaries (PDF) or list them explicitly. Add a regression test per form.

issues.problem: False positives that fail CI (check-repo-invariants.sh in the validate job, and test-no-personal-machine-paths.sh) on legitimate content: the Homebrew-on-Linux prefix /home/linuxbrew/, CI/container accounts (/home/codespace, /home/gitpod, /home/ec2-user, /home/vagrant, /home/jovyan, /home/pi, /home/circleci, /home/coder, C:\Users\runneradmin on GitHub Windows runners, C:\Users\Public, C:\Users\Default), retina asset names (logo@2x.png, icon@3x.webp parse as emails), ssh remotes git@gitlab.com: / git@bitbucket.org:, and vendor contacts such as security@anthropic.com. This is not hypothetical: the pending sibling package F2 adds '/home/linuxbrew/\.linuxbrew/bin/' to a hook regex, merges cleanly with H3b (git merge-tree rc=0), and then fails personal-data.
issues.evidence: REVF-H3b-probe/dec/pd/docs/fp.md (10 lines of legitimate content) -> 18 problems rc=1. git show fix/F2-input-analysis:hooks/lib/tool-input/shell_analysis.py > REVF-H3b-probe/dec/f2fix/... ; repo_invariants.py personal-data REVF-H3b-probe/dec/f2fix -> 'hooks/lib/tool-input/shell_analysis.py:1083: personal home-directory path' rc=1.
issues.suggested_fix: Add the well-known system/CI/container accounts (linuxbrew, runneradmin, public, default, codespace, gitpod, ec2-user, vagrant, jovyan, pi, circleci, coder, ...) to GENERIC_HOME_NAMES; exclude image extensions as email TLDs (png, jpg, jpeg, gif, svg, webp); treat git@<any host>: as an ssh remote; consider a reviewed allowlist file for vendor contact addresses. Add honest-variant tests for each, and run the check over the F2 branch before merging.

issues.problem: Pre-tag state: Step 5c pushes the release commit, whose .claude-plugin/marketplace.json now says ref vX, and the tag is pushed only after release CI and the RC matrix. Throughout that window (indefinitely if CI is red) the default branch advertises a ref that does not exist, so new installs or updates through the in-repo marketplace (README's primary '/plugin install alo-exp/silver-bullet' route) fail. Codex and Cursor already had this window; it now covers the primary Claude route and is not documented.
issues.evidence: Static: sync-marketplace-version.sh prepare mode writes ref v<version> without a tag (test 'no tag yet: no sha pinned' confirms); release skill order is 5b.1 sync -> 5c commit+push -> 6/6b CI -> 7 tag+push.
issues.suggested_fix: Document the window in docs/RELEASE.md and the release skill, or change the order: push the release commit to a release branch, wait for green CI, tag and push the tag, then fast-forward the default branch.

issues.problem: The docs say sync-codex-marketplace-version.sh writes source.sha once tagged and that --publish always writes both ref and sha, and the CHANGELOG says the Codex entry is pinned 'plus sha once tagged'. The Codex script writes only version and ref, in both modes.
issues.evidence: grep -n sha scripts/sync-codex-marketplace-version.sh -> no write of .source.sha; the publish jq program sets .version and .source.ref only.
issues.suggested_fix: Either write the tag commit sha in the Codex publish path (if Codex url sources accept it) or scope the docs and CHANGELOG to Claude and Cursor.

issues.problem: Incomplete r3 fix: only paths with a hooks/ or scripts/ component are rejected. A project-relative command chained after a valid plugin script still passes: '&& bash ./tools/evil.sh', '&& bash "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.githooks/x"', '; python3 evil.py', '&& source .envrc', '&& make -f Makefile', '$(cat x)'.
issues.evidence: REVF-H3b-probe/dec/hookref fixture, --check hook-references: those 6 commands -> PASS; './hooks/evil.sh', '$PWD/hooks/evil.sh', '${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/scripts/evil.sh' -> FAIL.
issues.suggested_fix: Allowlist as r3 suggested: each command must be exactly bash/sh "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/<existing file>" plus plain arguments, matching all 96 real commands.

issues.problem: Flow-style variants still evade the hardening check, base and head alike: 'steps:' with the flow sequence on the next line ('[ {run: "echo ${{ ... }}", continue-on-error: true} ]'), a flow-mapping top-level 'jobs: {...}', an anchored or tagged flow step ('- &s {...}', '- !!map {...}'), and 'continue-on-error : true' (space before the colon).
issues.evidence: python3 -I REVF-H3b-probe/dec/scan/wfprobe.py: steps_flow_on_next_line, jobs_flow_toplevel, anchor_flow_step, tagged_flow_step, space_before_colon -> head [] (base [] too).
issues.suggested_fix: Outside run scripts and block scalars, reject any line whose first non-space character is '[' or '{', any '- ' item followed by '&', '*' or '!', and any key:value whose value starts with '[' or '{' under jobs:; allow optional spaces before ':' in CONTINUE_ON_ERROR.

issues.problem: refresh-skills-lock hashes every file on disk (rglob), but vendored-skills-lock hashes only tracked files. An ignored or untracked file in a skill directory (.DS_Store from Finder, a local gitignored .claude/skills/<mine>/) gives a lock that the check rejects, and the error hint sends the maintainer back to the same refresh.
issues.evidence: REVF-H3b-probe/dec/lock (git repo with .gitignore '.DS_Store' and '.claude/skills/mine/'): refresh then check rc=0; after a .DS_Store in .claude/skills/graphify: refresh rc=0 then check '...content does not match ... (refresh with: ...)' rc=1; with an ignored .claude/skills/mine: refresh 'locked .claude/skills/mine' then check '.claude/skills/mine: listed in skills-lock.json toolManaged but missing' rc=1.
issues.suggested_fix: Have refresh use tracked_files(root) (falling back to the disk walk only for a non-git fixture), the same source as the check.

issues.problem: Performance: the EMAIL regex takes 20.5 s on graphify-out/graph.json alone; the full personal-data check takes 42-47 s wall (22-24 s CPU) and runs in CI's 'fast' validate job, in test-no-personal-machine-paths.sh and in test-check-repo-invariants.sh.
issues.evidence: python3 -I REVF-H3b-probe/dec/scan/perf.py: UNIX_OR_WINDOWS_HOME 2.33 s, DASHED_HOME 1.75 s, EMAIL 20.5 s on graph.json; 'time repo_invariants.py personal-data .' -> real 46.9 s.
